title: Scaling Hybrid Quantum-HPC Applications with the Quantum Framework
problem: Hybrid Q-HPC workflows must select best simulator for each circuit type; no single simulator optimal for all
motivation: NISQ devices require flexible execution across diverse simulators; backend selection critical for performance but circuit-dependent
method: The Extended Quantum Framework provides a single programming interface to five quantum computing backends: Qiskit Aer, NWQ-Sim, QTensor, and TN-QVM (which run on local machines) and IonQ (which runs on remote cloud hardware). When you submit a quantum circuit, you can explicitly choose which backend to use, or let the system select based on circuit characteristics. The payoff is that different simulators use different internal strategies and perform better on different types of circuits, so having easy access to all of them lets you pick the best one for your specific problem.
key_novelty: The framework lets users swap between different quantum simulators and cloud providers without rewriting code, revealing which backend is best for different circuit types.
contributions: Unified interface for diverse quantum backends
limitations: Limited to NISQ capabilities; backend availability constraints
